title: Deprecation playbook for legacy v2 model API + migration roadmap
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Sunset the legacy /v2/model inference endpoint and migrate users to the unified /v3/model endpoint with feature parity and lower latency. This ticket owns the cross-functional plan: comms timeline, migration guide, release notes, support playbook, and tracking metrics.

Scope:
- Public API: /v2/model (text generation, chat) will be deprecated. Not in scope: embeddings endpoints or Dedicated private endpoints unless explicitly listed in dependencies.
- Migration target: /v3/model with compatibility shim for common params and explicit mapping for changed fields.

High-level timeline:
- Mar 10, 2026: Publish Migration-Guide draft (Confluence) and Release Notes draft (Drive).
- Mar 17–24: Internal reviews (Eng, Design, Docs, Legal).
- Apr 1: Customer beta migration window announced for early adopters; opt-in telemetry enabled.
- Apr 15: Start automatic deprecation header injection (warn users on /v2 responses).
- May 15: Hard-deprecation: requests to /v2 will receive 410 with migration helper payload.
- May 30: Close monitoring and rollback window ends.

Migration guide deliverables (links and owners):
- Migration quickstart (GitHub gist + sample requests) — owner: Mateo Garcia — link: https://docs.internal.redwood/migrations/v2-to-v3-quickstart
- Compatibility table (param mapping, behavior diffs) — owner: Lina Cho (Docs) — link: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/API/V2+to+V3+Compatibility
- SDK patches list and PRs (Python/JS/Go) — owner: Eng SDK team (ENG-3854) — GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pulls?q=label%3Amigration-v3

Comms plan and channels:
- Release notes: Draft in Drive — editor: Aisha Patel — link: https://drive.redwood.com/release-notes/api-deprecations-may-2026
- Developer blog post: product marketing to draft with technical appendix. Channel schedule: blog + email to registered API keys list + in-console banner.
- In-console banners: short warning when projects call /v2; link to migration guide. Designer: DES-214.
- Customer success outreach: high-usage customers flagged via telemetry will receive 1:1 migration assistance.

Rollout mechanics and fallback:
- Step 1: Soft warnings — add Deprecation-Warning header and telemetry events for any /v2 call.
- Step 2: Beta phase — opt-in automatic redirects to /v3 for eligible calls, measure error delta.
- Step 3: Hard-deprecation — 410 responses with JSON body containing migration steps and link to one-click SDK migration tool.
- Rollback: If error rate on /v3 increases >5% for >30m across top 10 customers, revert redirect and open incident (ENG on-call).

Metrics and success criteria:
- Migration adoption: 80% of active projects on /v2 migrate to /v3 before May 1.
- Error delta: migration should not increase 5xx rate by >0.5% aggregate.
- Docs uptake: migration guide pageviews >= 2000 in first 30 days.
- Support load: CS tickets related to migration should be < 4/week after beta phase.

Artifacts to produce before Apr 1:
- Finalized migration guide (Docs)
- Release notes + blog draft
- In-console banner copy and art (DES-214)
- SDK PR checklist and one-click migration scripts
- Support playbook and canned responses for Tier 1/2

Stakeholders / RACI:
- Product (R): Aisha Patel — overall plan, comms
- Engineering (A): Mateo Garcia — migration tooling, telemetry, redirects
- Docs (R): Lina Cho — migration guide
- Design (C): DES-214 — banners and in-console flow
- SDK (A): ENG-3854 — SDK compatibility and PRs
- CS & Sales (I): Priya Nair — customer outreach
- Legal (C): review on deprecation terms and API contract language

Notes on compatibility decisions (tradeoffs documented):
- We will not preserve legacy 'stop_sequences' array semantics that are ambiguous; instead migration guide provides deterministic mapping and examples.
- Quantization and runtime hints: v3 exposes new kernel flags; automatic redirect will surface a warning if config mismatch is likely to alter tokenization outcomes.

Links to drafts and trackers:
